Getting Started

Overview

LandMarker is a desktop application for registering 3D medical images. It supports automated, landmark-based, and intensity-based registration workflows, and allows users to interactively place corresponding landmarks on moving and fixed images.

Supported Files

Image loading currently supports NIfTI images, including .nii and .nii.gz files.

Before You Start

  • Have moving and fixed image files ready.
  • Choose where landmark files and registered images should be saved.
  • Use GPU registration only when a compatible GPU environment is available.

Basic Workflow

  1. Load a moving image.
  2. Load a fixed image.
  3. Load overlay images if desired.
  4. Make adjustments to image display (colormap, windowing, etc.).
  5. Select the compute device and registration algorithm.
  6. Create or load corresponding landmarks, if using landmark-based registration.
  7. Run registration and review the registered result.
  8. Save the registered image and deformation field as needed.
  9. Load additional moving images and apply deformation field.
  10. Save additional registered images.

Image I/O

Load a Moving Image

  1. Select Moving Image > Load NIfTI.
  2. In the file selection dialog, browse to and select the NIfTI image file to load.
  3. If the image contains binary values (such as a mask) or discrete integer labels (such as a segmentation), select Load as segmentation (label map).
  4. Click Open.

Note: LandMarker currently supports only the NIfTI image format (.nii and .nii.gz).

Load a Fixed Image

  1. Select Fixed Image > Load NIfTI.
  2. In the file selection dialog, browse to and select the fixed NIfTI image file (.nii or .nii.gz).
  3. For a binary mask or an image containing discrete integer segmentation labels, check Load as segmentation (label map).
  4. Click Open.

Note: LandMarker currently supports only the NIfTI image format (.nii and .nii.gz).

Load a Moving Overlay

  1. Select Moving Image > Load Overlay NIfTI.
  2. Browse to and select the NIfTI overlay file.
  3. Click Open to load the moving overlay.

Load a Fixed Overlay

  1. Select Fixed Image > Load Overlay NIfTI.
  2. Browse to and select the NIfTI overlay file.
  3. Click Open to load the fixed overlay.

Save a Moving Image

  1. Select Moving Image > Save NIfTI.
  2. In the file dialog, navigate to the desired destination folder and enter a file name.
  3. Click Save to save the moving image.

Save a Fixed Image

  1. Select Fixed Image > Save NIfTI.
  2. In the file dialog, navigate to the desired destination folder and enter a file name.
  3. Click Save to save the fixed image.

Save a Registered Image

  1. Select Registered Image > Save NIfTI.
  2. In the file dialog, navigate to the desired destination folder and enter a file name.
  3. Click Save to save the registered image.

View Image Information

To view image metadata, select View Image Info from the menu for the desired image:

  • Moving Image > View Image Info
  • Fixed Image > View Image Info
  • Registered Image > View Image Info

The Image Header Information window displays metadata such as file information, data type and range, image dimensions, voxel spacing, coordinate system convention, image origin, and direction cosines.

Scroll within the window to view additional information, and click Close when finished.

Landmarks

What is a Landmark?

A landmark is a point representing the same anatomical feature in two images. Each landmark is associated with two images and stores the coordinates of that point within each image.

Landmarks are displayed as red dots on the images. When a landmark is selected, it is highlighted in green. Landmark coordinates are displayed in the Landmarks tables in the main window.

Matching Image Geometry

Before creating landmarks, the moving and fixed images must have matching geometry: the same shape, origin, and resolution.

If the currently displayed images do not have matching geometry, the Resample button in the upper-right corner of the main window is yellow and the Register button is disabled. When the images have matching geometry, the Resample indicator is green, the Register button is enabled, and the images are outlined with a thin green line.

To match their geometries, click the Resample button to resample the moving image to the fixed image geometry. Save the resampled moving image if desired.

Create a Landmark

  1. Click New below the Landmarks table for either the moving or fixed image. Either New button can be used.
  2. Navigate to the anatomical feature in either image where you want to place the landmark. Hold down Ctrl and left-click to place the point. The landmark-in-progress appears as a green point.
  3. Navigate to the corresponding anatomical feature in the other image and hold down Ctrl while left-clicking to place the matching point. A landmark requires a point in both images.
  4. Before saving, adjust either point if necessary by holding down Ctrl and clicking and dragging it. A point can only be moved within the current slice.
  5. Click Save below either image's Landmarks table to complete the landmark.

Selecting a Landmark

To select a landmark, click its row in either Landmarks table, or hold down the Ctrl key and left-click the landmark in an image.

Edit a Landmark

  1. Select the landmark you wish to edit.
  2. Click Edit below either Landmarks table. The selected landmark enters edit mode and is displayed as a green dot.
  3. Hold down the Ctrl key and click and drag the point to its new location. You may edit the point in either image or both corresponding image points.
  4. When satisfied with the landmark's position, click Save.

Delete a Landmark

To delete a landmark, select the landmark, then click Delete below either Landmarks table.

Save Landmarks

To save landmarks, select Landmarks > Save to file.

Landmarks created in LandMarker can be saved to a pair of files named source.mrk.json and target.mrk.json.

You may select the directory where these files are saved, but their file names cannot be changed.

The files follow the JSON Schema Draft-07 schema.

Import Landmarks

LandMarker can import landmarks from a previously saved LandMarker file pair or from individual JSON files generated by another program.

Import a LandMarker File Pair

  1. Select Landmarks > Load from Landmarker file pair.
  2. Navigate to the folder containing source.mrk.json and target.mrk.json.

Import Individual JSON Files

  1. Select Landmarks > Import Individual json files.
  2. When prompted, select the landmarks file for the moving image.
  3. When prompted again, select the landmarks file for the fixed image.

Registration

Select a Registration Algorithm

To select a registration algorithm, open the Registration menu in the main window. Choose Landmark-Based Algorithms or Intensity-Based Algorithms to access the available methods.

Select CPU or GPU

If a GPU is available, you can use it to speed up the registration process. To select the compute device, choose Registration > Device from the main window menu, then select the desired device.

Run Registration

  1. Click the Register button in the main window to start registration.
  2. Depending on the selected algorithm, you may be prompted to specify additional parameters. Enter the parameters and click OK.
  3. When registration is complete, the newly registered image automatically appears in the bottom row of viewports, overlaid on the fixed image.

Adjust Registered Overlay

One way to evaluate the quality of the registration is to compare the registered image overlay with the underlying fixed image.

Use the slider to the left of the registered-image viewports to alpha blend the images. Moving the slider increases the transparency of one image while decreasing the transparency of the other, allowing you to compare their alignment.
